title: Algenta integration tool-profile contract
description: Every framework-integration package in this repository (pydantic-ai, LangChain, LiteLLM,
TypeScript/JS tool-calling helpers, and anything added later) must map Algenta's MCP tool
surface onto a model-facing 'tool profile' that conforms to this document. A package MUST
NOT invent its own profile boundaries, its own default profile, or its own name for a tool
already named here. scripts/check-parity.py and scripts/check-parity.ts exist to verify that
every language's package actually agrees with this file (they are stubs today; D1+ fills
provenance_note: Tool names below are Algenta's public MCP tool-registry names, exactly as exposed over
stdio/HTTP/`/mcp/*` by a self-hosted Algenta Engine (verified against the engine's own
MCP tool registry vocabulary and its published examples/ integration snippets, which are
part of the public protocol surface). This file contains no engine implementation and no
engine source of any kind -- only the already-public tool names and the JSON-Schema shape
of the safety-relevant fields on the execute-tier tool. A tool NAME and its request/response
SCHEMA are the public interface; the code that implements them is not, and is not present
self_hosted_only_note: Every tool in every profile below is called against the CALLER'S OWN self-hosted Algenta
Engine over HTTP or MCP at request time (see ALGENTA_BASE_URL / self-hosted `/mcp`).
No package in this repository bundles, embeds, or talks to a hosted-by-Algenta engine

description: Some model-calling frameworks (e.g. OpenAI/Azure Assistants function calling) require a
single flat, globally-unique tool name and do not support MCP-style namespacing. When an
integration package must flatten a tool for such a framework, it MUST prefix the MCP tool
name with 'algenta_' (e.g. MCP tool 'get_contract' -> external tool name 'algenta_get_contract';
MCP tool 'query_data' -> 'algenta_query_dataset' or similar). This convention is already used
in the engine's own published framework examples (see e.g. an Azure AI Studio integration's
must follow it rather than inventing a different flattened name per framework.

get_contract.description: Fetch the live, machine-readable capability/discovery contract for the connected engine. Always call this before other tools that depend on discovering datasets or capabilities.

query_data.description: Run one governed exact query (or an exact-query batch) against an authorized, connected dataset.

simulate.description: Run a Monte Carlo / decision simulation over a scenario definition and return a decision envelope (recommendation, confidence, metrics).

recommend.description: Return a governed recommendation for a decision scenario without a full simulation run.

plan_decision.description: Produce a proposed, not-yet-committed decision plan (plan_hash included) for human or downstream governance review.

log_decision.description: Persist a decision record (and its rationale) to decision memory for audit and later outcome recording. Does not execute anything.

execute_decision.description: Dispatch one already-planned, already-logged decision for real-world execution (e.g. a webhook delivery) and persist the execution receipt.

observe.description: Read-only situational awareness. The default profile for every integration package unless a caller explicitly opts into a higher profile.

govern.description: Adds the ability to propose and record decisions, without ever executing them.

execute.description: Adds real-world execution of an already-planned, already-logged decision. This profile MUST NOT be enabled by default and MUST NOT be reachable by a model without every gate below satisfied.
requires_all_of: explicit server-side enablement (the self-hosted engine operator has turned execute-tier tools on for this API key/role -- an integration package cannot itself turn this on)
caller role/permission check passes on the engine side
an out-of-band policy approval already recorded against the plan_hash being executed
a caller-supplied idempotency key on the execute_decision call
the plan_hash of an already-planned (plan_decision) and already-logged (log_decision) decision -- execute_decision may not originate a new, unplanned action
a single-use nonce, to make replay of a captured execute_decision call a no-op on the engine side
execute.never_model_facing_note: These two fields exist on execute_decision's schema for operator/break-glass use only. No integration package may expose them as a parameter the model can set -- not in a tool schema, not via a kwarg the model's function-call arguments can reach, not via a default that resolves to true. If a human operator needs to set them, that happens outside the model-facing tool call entirely.

full.description: Opt-in complete tool registry (all ~117 MCP tools across all 12 categories: data onboarding, data access, schema discovery, query & ingest, LLM utilities, runtime libraries, decisions, agent runtime, control plane, observability, decision memory, triggers). Intended for admin/ops tooling and advanced users, never a model-facing default.

conformance.description: A framework-integration package conforms to this contract if, for every supported profile, the set of tools it exposes to the model matches this file's 'tools'/'adds_tools' exactly (no additions, no omissions), the default profile is 'observe' unless the caller explicitly requests otherwise, and 'execute' is never reachable without all of 'requires_all_of' being enforced server-side.
